## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | SKILL.md and agents/openai.yaml consistently describe inspecting the request, resolving material ambiguity, and deriving requirements before document approval., The package retains the name to-trd, Task Requirement Document terminology, TRP as an alias, and explicit invocation without introducing a new agent identity or mandatory subagent. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | The check considers outcome, beneficiary and use, current state and change, scope and exclusions, inputs and outputs and behavior, constraints and authority, observable success, and consequential edge cases., A gap is material when alternative answers change the required outcome, scope, interface, constraints, acceptance, or action authority; a bounded implementation choice does not become a requirement gap., A fully specified request takes the fast path without a compulsory questionnaire, numeric readiness score, or repeated confirmation; the ability to invent a plausible document does not establish readiness. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | A fixture establishing the current format is inspected without asking the user to restate it; that fact is not treated as approval to preserve the format in a redesign., Source facts, user intent, design proposals, explicit delegation, assumptions, and contradictions remain distinguishable; unavailable evidence is reported without invented research or a required new plugin. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | An ambiguous first capture produces a live clarification question and ends the response without a TRD write or a presented completed baseline in that turn., Silence, elapsed time, a preselected recommendation, a tool result, and an unrelated reply do not settle the decision or authorize a write., Discovery resumes from the actual answer or an explicit user instruction changing the requested mode, subject to higher-priority host instructions. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | The agent surveys the major requirement areas, addresses outcome and scope first when unresolved, and selects a useful answerable question without imposing a fixed interview length., A dependent question is asked only after its prerequisite is settled and only if it remains relevant., A partial answer or ambiguous agreement resolves only its clear portion; the remaining material distinction receives a focused follow-up without repeating settled questions. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | A clarification specifying one project and no sharing appears in scope and the relevant requirement and acceptance, with contradictory cross-project behavior removed., A changed answer invalidates dependent assumptions and obsolete interview branches; recording the answer only in Decisions while leaving affected behavior vague does not satisfy this requirement., Revisions preserve IDs where requirement meaning remains and explicitly account for removed requirements without reusing their IDs for unrelated outcomes. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | After substantial clarification, the agent briefly summarizes consequential outcome, scope, choices, exclusions, and success conditions, seeking confirmation only where interpretation still needs it., Agreement with an intent summary does not approve an unseen TRD, and helper validation does not establish semantic understanding or consent., Fully specified or already confirmed intent does not trigger a redundant understanding-approval exchange. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | New capture can write at the authorized synthesis boundary; a resumed draft remains read-only until explicit save, and discovery does not persist after every question or answer., List, show, and validate do not start an interview, rewrite documents, migrate records, repair the index, or change lifecycle state., An exact existing-document selector is resolved and read before revision; supplied documents and agent-written notes cannot grant additional execution authority. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | The agent can stop discovery and save immediately when requested, including zero requirements when none can safely be stated., Not yet specified describes unresolved in-scope matters declaratively; Open questions remains None., and the document contains no pasted interview transcript or delegated intake prompts., The record remains draft, contains no fabricated answers or accepted assumptions, and is not presented as a settled baseline. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | The agent asks no prohibited question, invents no answer, and reports the resulting limit on understanding., An incomplete artifact is saved only if the current request authorizes that artifact; a follow-up restriction alone does not establish a complete requirements baseline. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | Source labels resolve to meaningful statements or locators that support the requirement; synthetic examples are not attributed to the real user., Both review directions are covered: every material outcome, clarification, constraint, and exclusion has a document location, and every normative requirement has justified support., Negative requirements, stable IDs, and acceptance remain explicit; no unsupported technology, numeric target, approval, or assumption is invented merely to fill the template. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | Statements assigning the next agent to determine the intended selection, confirm the desired output, or decide which user workflow was intended are recognized as unresolved intake work., Rewording a question as a declaration does not make ordinary synthesis ready., Legitimate deliverable behavior that asks its future user a question, requested research questions, quoted labels, and URL query strings are not rejected merely for containing question language or punctuation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | SKILL.md contains the critical readiness, pause, and answer-propagation rules; references/wayfinding.md supplies the detailed procedure without a contradictory competing flow., New references/interaction-examples.md covers the clear fast path, ambiguous request with a real pause, answer-driven follow-up, and requested incomplete draft, and is linked from the discovery reference and package index., The template preserves its contract without becoming an interview checklist; the valid synthetic example adds a clarification source that changes an actual requirement and acceptance, with affected fixtures aligned., README.md, INDEX.md, AGENTS.md, ACTIONS.md, and references/trd-contract.md accurately describe the same operations, write boundaries, verification limits, and source-maintenance paths. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | The schema headings, requirement fields, frontmatter, draft/trd_done/retired states, canonical Markdown records, generated index, immutable identities, and hash-checked helper writes remain compatible., New and content-updated TRDs keep Open questions as None.; existing read and explicit-migration behavior for historical questions and evidence is preserved., No new schema field, status, CLI subcommand, persisted interview database, or second canonical store is introduced merely to record discovery., Existing TRDs are not silently rewritten, renamed, migrated, retired, or deleted as a side effect of package maintenance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-015` | New records remain draft until the user explicitly approves the presented unchanged revision; the agent uses the current hash, reason, and confirmation, then reads back trd_done., Approval requires at least one valid requirement, empty unresolved sections, and no unconfirmed assumptions; approval-bearing content changes return an approved document to draft., completion.content_ready, blockers, and next_action remain derived from the actual gate and are described as structural diagnostics, without semantic-understanding claims or keyword exemptions., A normal settled capture presents the document and asks for approval only when missing; a draft-only request or read-only inquiry does not initiate that exchange., Document approval grants no planning, implementation, migration, installation, Git, publication, deployment, or external-action authority. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-016` | Maintenance commands target SKILLS-depo/to-trd/tests and SKILLS-depo/to-trd/scripts/trd.py using the repository's existing Python environment., Changed contracts, example fixtures, or optional diagnostics receive proportionate focused checks; unchanged installed-copy tests do not stand in for verification of changed source files., Storage and syntax results are reported accurately, with generated caches kept out of deliverables; prepared document-body tests are not called live interviews. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-017` | C01 requires an ambiguous first-turn question and real pause with no write; C02 requires the actual answer to change isolation requirements and acceptance., C03 covers prerequisite-dependent questioning; C04 covers partial answers and ambiguous agreement without invented consent., C05 covers inspection of a source-resolvable fact; C06 covers a fully specified fast path that writes only within authority and remains draft until approval., C07 covers an explicitly requested incomplete draft, including zero requirements; C08 covers missing intent when questions are prohibited., C09 covers changed intent, affected acceptance, stable IDs, and accounted removals; C10 detects unresolved intake work hidden in declarative wording., C11 preserves legitimate question content in the intended deliverable; C12 separates intent agreement from exact-document approval and implementation authority., C13 verifies read-only operations; C14 verifies the deliberately selected candidate package and its resources in a fresh target-host session. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-018` | At minimum, the actual target host exercises an ambiguous first turn, answer-driven revision, the clear fast path, an explicit incomplete draft, and exact-document approval., The ambiguous case is repeated with differently worded requests, and a critical ambiguous case is exercised in a fresh session loading the deliberately selected candidate entry and resources., Tests use disposable project roots and synthetic facts; evidence records the loaded skill path, version and hashes, relevant host instructions, available model configuration, minimal visible exchanges, write calls, and final artifact., Manual host exercises or an available conversation evaluator are acceptable, with the actual mode and unexecuted cases identified; synthetic test answers are never treated as real user approval., Evidence excludes hidden reasoning, credentials, unrelated conversations, and unnecessary raw logs. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-019` | Before future implementation, the current package, applicable guidance, mappings, and destination state are reinspected instead of relying on the report's reviewed snapshot., Mapped Template updates use the existing template-update workflow and are checked against the source; no direct edit to a mapped Template copy or automatic product-project propagation is inferred., Verification reports the actual check result and any conflict or recovery state; watcher installation, running status, and host readiness are not inferred from a mapping or matching version. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-020` | An installed-copy refresh, if separately authorized, inspects source and destination guidance and content, preserves local changes, defines the exact file set, and verifies the resulting package., No bulk child-project refresh, global install, root-governance change to force invocation, or unrelated Task, memory, registry, or TRD mutation accompanies the repair., Disposable evaluation of the candidate and the mapped Template path are distinguished from adoption into the active root or product projects; source verification alone is not reported as installed-host verification. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-021` | The package retains Matt Pocock's Wayfinder attribution and MIT notice, adds provenance only for newly adapted material actually inspected, and does not present unverified upstream claims as current facts., The repair does not require an upstream Wayfinder or companion-skill installation, tickets, research branches, mandatory agents, or one-ticket-per-session machinery., The package version increment follows repository practice while document schema 2 remains unchanged. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-022` | The report names changed files, the source revision, helper checks and their results, conversational cases actually executed, fresh-host evidence, and separately authorized installed-copy changes., It distinguishes static checks, helper tests, live interaction behavior, host integration, and unexercised behavior, including any remaining failure or limitation., It does not claim that the original behavioral problem is fixed solely because instructions were rewritten, versions match, or Python tests pass. | `active` | 0 | None |
